title: Apollo Tyres Ltd - 500877 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Apollo Tyres Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 14% to INR 73.4 bn with 14.6% EBITDA margin, while India and Europe face a steep raw-material cost push.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 14% YoY to INR 73.4 bn and EBITDA margin was 14.6% versus 13% a year ago, despite roughly INR 100 crore of extra cricket-jersey sponsorship and activation spend. India revenue rose 14.3% to INR 52.4 bn on high-teens volume growth in both replacement and OE, with a 14.6% margin. Europe revenue fell 1% to EUR 170 mn, with EBITDA of EUR 25 mn (14.6% margin), and the Enschede plant closure carried a EUR 43 mn non-cash write-off. Management guided to a sharp raw-material cost increase (mid to high teens QoQ in Q1) and is taking two rounds of price hikes totalling 6-8%, with more needed.

segments.name: India Operations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 52.4 bn (+14.3% YoY), EBITDA INR 7.6 bn at 14.6% margin; high-teens volume growth in OE and replacement, TBR replacement up 20%+ and PCR replacement single-digit OE/high-single to 20%+ per management split. Capacity utilisation about 90%.

segments.name: Europe Operations
segments.commentary: Revenue EUR 170 mn (-1% YoY) on muted market; passenger car outperformed market while truck supply was hit by India supply issues. EBITDA EUR 25 mn at 14.6% margin vs 14.3%.

guidance_outlook: Raw material costs expected to rise mid to high teens sequentially in Q1 FY27; Q2 could be marginally higher than Q1 if current levels persist.
Price hikes of 6-8% announced for Q1 FY27 in India (3-5% implemented, rest in May); at least two more rounds needed beyond this to offset cost push.
India margins to remain under pressure in near term; management expects margin normalisation with pricing catch-up over time.
A&P spend to normalise at around 2.5% plus of sales from 4% in Q4 FY26 (typical 2%).
Enschede plant last production day June 30, 2026; positive European margin impact expected from H2 FY27.
FY27 consolidated capex of INR 35 bn, about 80% growth/capacity; roughly INR 3,000 crore India, balance Europe (mainly Hungary passenger car expansion).
Europe cash outflow of about EUR 50 mn in FY27 for social plan; total cash provision of EUR 55 mn-plus already taken.
Europe blended tax rate about 20%; India 25% from FY27.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex outlined at INR 35 bn, with nearly 80% towards growth and capacity expansion.
India capex close to INR 3,000 crore of the INR 3,500 crore (per transcript figures) covering truck and car tyre capacity expansion.
Hungary plant: passenger car tyre expansion already well underway; no truck expansion there.
Capacity utilisation at about 90% across India and Europe; management expects full utilisation and continues planned expansion.
Management said FY27 is largely committed for the previously announced large capex plan; some flexibility exists for FY28 if demand slows.
Export volumes to be deprioritised in favour of home markets India and Europe given tight capacity, especially in truck tyres.
demand_pricing: India volume growth high teens YoY in both OE and replacement in Q4; sequential volume growth about 2% QoQ, which accounted for all of the 2% QoQ revenue growth.
Standalone exports up mid-single digits in Q4; US market weak, though price increases of mid to high single digits announced there.
Market share: management believes it gained share in TBR replacement for FY26 and in PCR replacement, but not in PCR OE; based on internal estimates.
Dealer inventory in India: no marked difference in levels.

Raw material costs: natural rubber INR 200/kg in Q4 rising to INR 250/kg currently; synthetic rubber INR 170, carbon black INR 110, steel cord INR 155 per kg in Q4. Blended RM basket up about 1% QoQ in Q4.
OEM contracts largely follow a formula with a three-month lag; some OEMs negotiated with only small increases so far.
Competition: all peers have announced price hikes, with Apollo and CEAT slightly ahead; management does not expect discounting-led aggressive pricing near term.
Europe: 2% price increase announced; Apollo is a price follower and waiting for competitors. Europe needs less than half the price increase India needs for the same raw-material rise.
Management expects April demand to be as strong as Q4, but second-half FY27 is uncertain given GDP downgrades and fuel/tyre inflation; new vehicle purchases likely to be deferred first.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Europe margins still well below pre-crisis levels, and what drove the restructuring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe margins were 16%+ historically but now 14-15% because of two years of flat to negative market, high energy costs and Dutch salary inflation of 12-13% a year versus a usual 4-5%. That led to the Enschede closure decision.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 commodity costs rise further and how much more price is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Current RM inflation is mid to high teens. About half of the needed price increase has been taken, so at least a couple more rounds are needed. If spot levels hold, Q2 could be marginally higher than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How much Europe revenue is at risk from the Enschede closure?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the agricultural/OHT category, about 12% of revenues in total, of which OE is about half (roughly 5-6%). Some OE business that was loss-making may be given up; other products will be supplied from Hungary or India.

qa_highlights.question: What cash outflows follow the Enschede closure in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About EUR 50 mn social plan payout in FY27, with EUR 55 mn-plus total cash provision already taken in earlier quarters; no further cash provision is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Does the standalone India entity benefit from rupee weakness on European exports?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Under transfer pricing, India retains only a fixed margin on exports to Europe, so the group benefits rather than the standalone entity. Management will use India's cost advantage for exports if it widens.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 capex flexible if demand slows?
qa_highlights.answer: Some flexibility exists, but FY27 is largely committed given utilisation near 90% and April struggles to keep up with demand. Flexibility is greater for FY28.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation of mid to high teens in Q1 and possibly higher in Q2 could compress India margins until price hikes catch up; OEM contracts lag by three months.
Demand sustainability in H2 FY27 as fuel and tyre inflation and GDP downgrades weigh on fleet operators and new vehicle purchases.
West Asia geopolitical volatility affecting raw materials, energy and logistics; US export market weak.
Europe recovery depends on market stabilising, Hungary ramp-up and Enschede transfer; EUR 50 mn social plan cash outflow in FY27.
Other operating income in Europe falls as Hungary state-aid amortisation moves out with TBR assets, which will weigh on reported European revenue over the next few quarters.
A&P spend normalisation to about 2.5% of sales from 4% in Q4; watch whether spend stays elevated.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and balance sheet but cautious on margins; management repeatedly called the cost and demand outlook "very volatile" and declined to predict Q2 margins or second-half demand.
key_quotes: Despite the tough macroeconomic environment, we expect to sustain and accelerate top-line growth in India and Europe.
Mid to high teens is the current reality. It can change because the situation, even as we have progressed, about a month and a half into the quarter, has kept changing.
We definitely believe that in a normalised scenario, we will get back to a 16% which was our earlier normal, and in fact, we believe we can even surpass that.
